selfCorrection.summary: Rider RB-DR011-V3-A3 corrects a misreference I not only failed to catch but quoted approvingly in my own v3 verdict. This is a fourth instance of my recorded pattern, and the purest form of it so far.
selfCorrection.whatIDid: v3's namedD055Consequences.R16 reads 'Product boundary stays on Route C (D-068 / D-010).' In my v3 verdict I listed this among the improvements, writing that R16 'gains the D-068 / D-010 attribution' — offering the citation as evidence that v3 was more specific than D-055. I did not check the identifier at all.
selfCorrection.whyItIsWrong: D-010 is a real decision in COORD, but it is 'Register content: the V1→V2 transition-contract row (V2TOPIC-F-02)' — nothing to do with the product boundary. The correct referent is DR-010, the register row that D-068 owner-records and that v3 itself pins correctly in operativeDispositionPins. So the same document uses both forms, one character apart, and I read past it.
selfCorrection.whyThisInstanceIsWorse: My three earlier recorded misses were failures to check what a citation resolved to. Here an existence check would not even have saved me — D-010 exists — and I performed no check at all, because the citation appeared in a passage I had already decided was a strength. Praising a field is not reviewing it.
selfCorrection.correctiveDiscipline: Two things. First, identifier families that differ only by prefix — D-nnn versus DR-nnn here, and the same hazard exists for R-nn versus DR-011-Rnn — must be checked against the referent's subject matter, never merely for existence, because both forms resolve. Second, any citation I am about to cite approvingly in a verdict gets checked before it goes in the verdict; a passage I have judged to be a strength is exactly where I stop reading adversarially, so it needs the check most.

otherReviewerDivergenceNoted: Rider RB-DR011-V3-A2 answers Codex's RB-DR011-CX-A1 on the residualsRemainOpen field naming — the same point I examined in my v2 review and explicitly declined to file, writing that I was 'reporting none rather than padding'. I do not think that call was wrong: nothing was false, file 08 itself describes R06 and R07's remaining halves as OPEN, and the rider does not correct the field but glosses it, confirming R06 and R07 stay NARROWED. But the gloss is a real improvement to a field that will be quoted into a register cell, and Codex filing it produced that improvement where my declining it would not have.
summary: Subject and prompt held at their dispatched digests, both read-only. The entry records v3 rather than the REJECTED v2, rejects that substitution by name, and carries all three advisories as riders rather than dropping or classifying them away. I checked each rider against what it answers: A1 restores exactly the two properties my own advisory named as lost and additionally repairs the dangling remeasurement clause by tying it to both the named properties and operativeDispositionPins; A2 glosses residualsRemainOpen as 'means not CLOSED' while holding R06 and R07 NARROWED with named OPEN halves and stating it does not promote them; A3 corrects the D-010 misreference to DR-010. None of the three grants anything. All five digests verify, my verdict recital is exact, and the D-039 / D-076 rider precedent is real.
whatIVerified: Prompt digest at start and end: c7765c7d42b80ddfca6e2603b1080fba10ff96162f2e69d6747d4923e5582034, equal to the dispatch-supplied value. Subject at 91fcdbb6e638b99d49ad7c139e9b8bc8a07afe48948335a4c98b5ce13ca94862, equal to both. Three measurements each at start and again at end; both -r--r--r-- at both ends.

The attack 'D-010 vs DR-010 left uncorrected' fails: rider A3 states that namedD055Consequences.R16 'cites **DR-010**, not D-010'. I verified the underlying defect independently — D-010 in COORD is the V1→V2 transition-contract register-content decision, unrelated to the product boundary, while DR-010 is the row D-068 owner-records and the row v3 pins correctly elsewhere. The correction is right.

The attack 'R06/R07 promoted' fails, and rider A2 is the guard. It reads 'residualsRemainOpen means not CLOSED. R06 and R07 stay **NARROWED** with named OPEN halves. This rider does not close or promote them.' That matches file 08, which records both rows as NARROWED with 'application half closed, validator-standing and join halves OPEN' and '…checker-standing and join halves OPEN'.

The attack 'riders invent a new grant' fails on all three. A1 is a pin restoration — it names four properties and extends the remeasurement clause. A2 is a definitional gloss on an existing field plus an explicit non-promotion. A3 is a one-identifier citation fix. None adds a surface, and clause 3 keeps 'Condition 1 does not discharge until the owners record v3 plus the three riders', so the riders bind the future owner recording rather than loosening it.

Rider A1 answers my advisory completely and slightly beyond it. My advisory recorded that v3 dropped propertyPins while keeping 'Pins support only the named properties', and that of v2's five named properties two — file 08's Exact DR-011 residual reconciliation and D-001's per-residual routes — appeared nowhere in v3. A1 restores both of those, plus D-018 naming and the D-081 condition-1 row, and then repairs the dangling clause directly: 'The remeasurement clause refers to those named properties plus operativeDispositionPins.' The one v2 item not restored, 'D-055 ADOPTED', is not lost — v3 carries D-055 in selectionAuthority and this entry pins the D-055 commit.

The attack 'records REJECTED v2' fails twice: clause 1 records v3 by path and digest f1c7f6b7…, and the alternatives section rejects the substitution by name — 'Record REJECTED v2. Rejected: RB-DR011-CX-B1.' The preamble states the history accurately: 'v2 was independently REJECTED (RB-DR011-CX-B1). v3 repairs that blocker. Both reviewers ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES, 0 blockers.'

The attack 'treats ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES as owner recording' fails: clause 1 states 'This is not owner recording. An ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES verdict is not owner recording and is not residual CLOSED', the header states 'Does not owner-record', and the alternatives reject the conflation by name.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED or residual CLOSED' fails: the header refuses SATISFIED and residual closure, clause 3 states 'DR-011 stays HARD-BLOCKED. Residuals stay not CLOSED', and the readiness effect is 'Zero.'

My verdict recital is exact, and this is the one I can verify absolutely: the entry cites my v3 verdict at 46ec1329a88fa428c5b964956361dd0ede2afdc09c61bdce924e806c67588b5d as 'ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES 0 blockers, RBDR011V3-C2-A1', and that file records exactly ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES, 0 blockers, 1 advisory under that id.

All five cited digests match live bytes: the v3 disposition f1c7f6b7…, my verdict 46ec1329…, the Codex verdict bd6a8c2f… (hashed, not opened), COORD d93614cd…, and file 08 1360a4f8…. The D-055 commit 5acba0fe… resolves to 'D-055: select Route B for DR-011 parent (preview scope)'.

The form citation is accurate and apt: D-039 and D-076 are both present in COORD and ADOPTED, and both are recordings that carry an operative rider alongside a disposition — RB-DR005-V2-A1 and RB-DR009-V2-A1 respectively. This is the third such recording and the first to carry three riders at once.

The rejected alternative for the riders is honest about the trade: 'Write a v4 just for the three advisories. Rejected this cycle: pin/wording, not a new grant. D-039 / D-076 precedent.' That characterisation holds for all three — a pin restoration, a gloss and a citation fix.

The attacks 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' and 'file 08 edited' fail: the header refuses the implementation directory, clause 3 preserves condition 5 as the only implementation authorization, clause 4 refuses the file 08 edit under MF-6, file 08 measures unchanged at its cited digest, and git reports zero changes under docs/v2/architecture.
D-082 is not yet present in COORD, so adoption creates no collision. I wrote one file and edited and committed nothing.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. The entry records the repaired v3 rather than the rejected v2, rejects that substitution by name, and carries all three advisories as riders that bind the future owner recording — none of which grants a surface. Rider A1 answers my own advisory in full and then goes past it, repairing the dangling remeasurement clause I flagged by tying it to both the restored properties and operativeDispositionPins. I have recorded a self-correction because rider A3 fixes a misreference I quoted approvingly in my v3 verdict: D-010 exists, which is why an existence check would not have caught it, and it is the V1→V2 transition-contract decision rather than the product-boundary row. The lesson I am taking is narrower and more useful than my earlier ones — prefix-distinguished identifier families must be checked against subject matter, and a citation I am about to praise is exactly the one I am least likely to have read.
